title: Why Busy Teams Still Fail | Principles of Management Ep 18
description:
It is festival week at Chai Corner. Everyone works flat out, yet cups go cold, the cash line stops and the helpers run out of clean cups. In this animated lesson, Ravi learns the two jobs that turn busy people into one team: directing and coordinating.

You will see what directing means (guiding people while they work) and its four parts: supervision, communication, leadership and motivation. Then we run the festival rush twice, without and with coordination, and watch a token system shrink the queue from 18 to 4. You will meet Mary Parker Follett (1868-1933) and the four principles of coordination from her lecture published in 1937: direct contact, early stages, reciprocal relating and a continuous process. We look at each idea at work today, from site supervisors and nurses' shift handovers to an airport getting a plane ready to fly again. And the human side: too much directing becomes micromanaging, and coordination gets harder as teams grow, because 4 people share 6 links but 10 people share 45.

This is Episode 18 of our Principles of Management series for MBA, BBA and commerce students.
